stories.notes: Command Center was already built (9 tabs under command-center/) against a separate hand-maintained plan; repointed DATA_DIR to .colaberry/ and added a root index.html redirect per this story's instructions. Verified via node --check on every script, a field-by-field trace of every plan.X/progress.X access against the real committed JSON, and running ownersFromPlan/verificationForRequirement in Node against the real data (owner breakdown matched the portal's own brief exactly). No live browser was available this session for a visual render check; see .colaberry/enrichment/STORY-000.json.

tests_added: pipeline/test_hcris_import.py (12 tests: state-prefix filtering, fiscal-year derivation from fy_end_dt not the download bucket, deterministic dedup tie-break, and the invalid-format failure path)
stories.notes: Real data: 256 OK/TX rural/CAH hospitals, 260 cost-report-years, live in Supabase, verified idempotent (identical content hash across two runs from a clean state). Every worksheet/line/column code cited against the CMS data dictionary and confirmed against a real downloaded report before being trusted. Two real bugs found by checking my own output rather than trusting the first run: a DuckDB lazy-evaluation bug (fixed by materializing pivots into real temp tables instead of reusing a shared view name) and a fiscal-year mislabeling bug (CMS's FY2024 download bucket is when CMS processed a report, not each report's own period end -- fixed by deriving fiscal_year from fy_end_dt). Only FY2024 has been run so far; STORY-002 (early-warning flags) and expanding to 3 years remain.

tests_added: pipeline/test_hcris_import.py (30 tests total, including the provider-scoped dedupe fixes found while backfilling provenance)
stories.notes: Criteria 2 and 3 were already genuinely true in the repo, built while hardening STORY-001: cost_report_years.operating_margin_pct/days_cash_on_hand/days_in_ar (REQ-002) are Postgres GENERATED ALWAYS AS STORED columns, so they can never drift from source_rpt_rec_num/source_file/metric_provenance. metric_provenance is a per-metric jsonb {wksht_cd, line_num, clmn_num, status} recording exactly which worksheet/line/column each value came from and whether it was ok/not_reported/unparseable -- live-backfilled across all 652 existing rows, 18 confirmed genuinely not_reported. Criterion 1 is left false on purpose: it asks for 'monthly metrics', but CMS HCRIS cost reports carry one annual figure per hospital fiscal year -- there is no month in this data source to slice. REQ-002 (the requirement this story fulfills) correctly says 'per hospital per year'; 'monthly metrics' is REQ-011/STORY-011's language (operator-uploaded monthly exports, release r2), and appears to have been copied into this story's acceptance criteria by mistake. Confirmed with the user before leaving it unticked rather than rewording or faking it.

tests_added: frontend/src/lib/hospitalSearch.test.ts (5 tests: name-search happy path, not-found returns an empty list rather than an error, and a data-retrieval error is surfaced as a typed result instead of thrown)

frontend/src/lib/hospitalDetail.test.ts (7 tests: three-years-ascending happy path, fewer-than-three-years without fabricating the gap, hospital-not-found short-circuits before querying years, data-retrieval errors from both the hospital and years lookups, and formatMetric never renders a missing value as zero or blank)
stories.notes: No Supabase client credentials (project URL + anon key) existed locally at the start of this story -- only DATABASE_URL, a direct Postgres connection string used by the Python pipeline. Considered querying Postgres directly from Next.js with that string instead of requesting a new credential, but rejected it: Vercel serverless functions are ephemeral and would exhaust Supabase's direct-connection limit under real traffic, which is exactly why Supabase fronts Postgres with a pooler and recommends the REST API / supabase-js for serverless clients. Got the anon/publishable key from the user instead (frontend/.env.local, gitignored) and built on supabase-js, which also matches this story's own task_guidance ('Next.js frontend ... with data from Supabase'). Search is case-insensitive partial-name match (ilike), not exact match, since public users won't know a hospital's exact CMS-registered name string -- a stricter reading of 'a hospital name' was considered and rejected as needlessly hostile to the actual user. Verified against live production data, not just mocks: a hospital with all three fiscal years (ST ANTHONY SHAWNEE HOSPITAL, CCN 370149) renders 2023/2024/2025 in order, and a hospital with a genuine gap (ANSON GENERAL HOSPITAL, CCN 670781, missing FY2023) renders only its real 2 years plus an explicit 'reporting gap, not an error' note rather than a fabricated third row. The 'notes public data lag' criterion is a static, honest disclosure about CMS's filing-and-processing delay, not a computed lag figure -- there is no per-row lag data in the source to compute one from, and inventing a number would violate the project's own grounding guardrail (REQ-004).

criteria.text: Given computed metrics, When flagging criteria are met, Then the system flags the hospital.
Given missing data, When flagging criteria are checked, Then the system marks the hospital as 'not assessable'.
Trust: Each flag stores the exact values that triggered it.

tests_added: pipeline/test_early_warning.py (10 tests: each of the 3 criteria genuinely triggering, a fully healthy hospital with real falling-AR data correctly not flagged, missing metrics marked not_assessable rather than silently cleared, a real trigger winning over an unrelated missing metric, fewer-than-3-years and a real non-consecutive reporting gap both correctly not_assessable for the AR-trend criterion, and a falling AR trend correctly not_triggered rather than not_assessable)
stories.notes: Missing data is never treated as 'no problem': a criterion whose required metric is null is 'not_assessable', not 'not_triggered', and a hospital is only reported 'not_flagged' overall if every criterion was actually checked -- an early-warning system that quietly clears a hospital it couldn't check would defeat its own purpose. Precedence is flagged > not_assessable > not_flagged, so a real trigger is never hidden behind an unrelated missing metric (verified live: CCN 123456-style case with a real trigger + a missing metric elsewhere still flags). 'Days in A/R rising two years in a row' requires three CONSECUTIVE fiscal years, not just the latest three rows on file -- a hospital with a real reporting gap (missing fiscal year, an already-known pattern in this dataset) is correctly not_assessable for this one criterion rather than comparing non-adjacent years as if they were adjacent, which would silently understate what 'two years in a row' actually means. Flags are stored as one current-state row per hospital (early_warning_flags, PK provider_ccn), replaced on each run via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, not appended as history -- re-running the evaluator is idempotent (verified live: ran twice against production, 274 rows before and after, no duplicates, identical distribution). Ran for real against all 274 hospitals in production Supabase: 257 flagged, 16 not assessable, 1 genuinely healthy (RICE MEDICAL CENTER, CCN 451312 -- 5.84% margin, 55.8 days cash, falling A/R). The high flag rate is a real finding about this population (rural/Critical Access hospitals nationally run on thin or negative margins), not a logic bug -- spot-checked individual hospitals' exact stored values against the flag verdict to confirm. Public read RLS on the new table, same as hospitals/cost_report_years: no management-company scoping exists yet since STORY-006 (row-level security) and STORY-005 (operator uploads, the thing that would actually need company-level scoping) aren't built. Reused the exact 'latest 3 fiscal years, ascending' query shape from frontend/src/lib/hospitalDetail.ts so the flag evaluator and the public Health Snapshot page can never disagree about which years count as 'the latest three'.

tests_added: pipeline/test_phi_guardrail.py (22 tests: header-based detection for all three REQ-009 categories -- patient names, birth dates, record numbers; an SSN-shaped-content fallback for a mislabeled column; false-positive avoidance on ordinary business dates; and the ingest gate proving rejection happens before storage and before the PHI value itself ever reaches the audit log)
stories.notes: REQ-009's own wording ('reject... before it is stored or logged') requires real gating behavior, not just a detector -- STORY-011's grounding_guardrail.py was built the same standalone way and stayed unticked until something actually calls it, so scan_file_for_phi() alone would not have earned these criteria. Added ingest_file_with_phi_gate(file_name, rows, store=, log_audit=): store is only called when the scan is clean, never for a rejected file (proven by test_gate_rejects_a_file_with_patient_names_before_storage / test_gate_rejects_a_file_with_birth_dates_before_storage asserting store was never called), and log_audit always receives a PhiAuditEntry naming the column and category that triggered rejection but never the row content itself (test_gate_audit_log_never_contains_the_raw_row_content, test_gate_birth_date_value_never_reaches_the_audit_log). store/log_audit are injected because the real Supabase write and logger do not exist yet (STORY-005, not started) -- STORY-005 plugs in the real implementations without changing this function. Two-layer detection: column-header match for all three categories (deterministic, matches how a real hospital-system export would label these fields) plus an SSN-content fallback for a column mislabeled with an innocuous header. Deliberately not attempted: generic content-based matching for names or dates by shape alone -- financial exports carry legitimate business dates (report date, posting date) and free text cannot reliably be classified as 'a name' without a model, so that would trade false rejections of clean ledger data for coverage the header check already provides in the realistic case; documented as a known limitation in the module docstring, not left silent.
